base:
Create ONE intermediate animation frame on true alpha transparency. Reference image 1 is START, reference image 2 is END of the SAME adult curly-haired conductor turning toward the viewer and inviting them down a webpage with his baton. Interpolate the pose, preserving identity, clothes and visible copper/espresso oil brushwork exactly. NOT a contact sheet, no additional people or objects.

Camera locked, 1672x941 landscape canvas and fixed character scale. Hair top around y110, head center around x835 y200, torso pivot around x850 y510, hips near x850 y800, lower thighs terminate in painterly edge around bottom y930. Head height about165px: do not zoom or enlarge face during turn. Keep the man adult with realistic proportions, never toy-like. Pale baton always in right hand and fully inside canvas. Stable dramatic but painted warm light, dark espresso suit and ivory shirt/cuffs. Same precise painterly style, not photographic, not bronze statue. No floor, scenery, musician, glow or shadow on backdrop; transparent alpha everywhere outside the single character. No labels. Preserve only organic bottom painted contour, clean natural silhouettes elsewhere.
POSE FOR THIS FRAME:

poses.pose: Early anticipation, only a small change from START. Fully rear-facing torso and head. Both upper arms drop about 8 degrees. Left hand drops slightly. Right baton hand drops slightly and baton inclines a little closer to horizontal, its tip swings down only a little. No face visible.

Still rear-facing, calmly lowering arms. Upper arms now about shoulder level, elbows bent softly; left hand at upper shoulder height, right baton hand at shoulder height. Baton still points diagonally up toward center but at a shallower angle than START. No face visible. Torso same upright back view.

Rear-facing with head JUST beginning to glance toward his turning side, toward the face orientation of END. Upper arms lowered another 12 degrees, elbows about lower rib height, forearms bent, hands near chest level. Baton right hand near lower shoulder height, baton approaching horizontal. Almost all back of head visible, a tiny hint of cheek at side.

Turn has begun, torso about 25 degrees from rear-facing toward END. Head glances farther around toward viewer, small sliver of cheek and nose visible. Elbows at ribs, both hands around chest level. Baton comes down to near horizontal, tip pointing toward screen right. Coat gently follows rotation, not flaring newly.

Quarter-turn transition, torso about 45 degrees away from original back view toward END. Face in partial side profile, still looking along turn. Both elbows relaxed close to ribs, right baton hand at lower chest; baton points screen right nearly horizontal. Left palm begins to open politely near sternum. Stable upright body.

Middle of turn, torso about 65 degrees from original rear view toward END. Head in clear side profile but eyes beginning to glance at viewer. Right baton hand moves modestly toward screen right and down to waist, baton points screen right with slight 10 degree downward slope. Left hand stays relaxed near sternum, palm slightly open. No dramatic lean.

Torso about 85 degrees from back view toward END, largely side-on. Head turning another 15 degrees toward viewer beyond torso, face recognizable as man in END. Right arm extends a little diagonally down toward screen right; hand at waist. Baton points down-right about 20 degrees. Left hand open near chest. Jacket naturally turns with torso.

Torso nearly in final three-quarter orientation, about 105 degrees from original rear view. Face now meets viewer gently, restrained welcoming expression identical to END. Right forearm extends down-right but less than END; baton tip about x1190 y700. Left hand open near torso. Body scale and center stable.

Almost final orientation, torso matches END nearly fully, head meets viewer. Right arm reaches down-right to guide visitor, about 80 percent of final extension; baton tip near x1240 y780. Left palm relaxed open near chest, matching END. Coat settles into END folds.

Immediately before END: same final three-quarter torso, same face looking at viewer, same gentle expression. Right guiding arm 95 percent extended; right hand and baton a few pixels higher than END, baton tip near x1290 y840. Left hand and jacket nearly match END. This must be a tiny step from END, no scale or head-size change.

corrections.5: Edit the reference into the next animation pose of the SAME man. Preserve EXACT canvas, camera distance, identity, warm copper/espresso oil paint style, clothes, alpha transparency and lower body scale. Single pose on original 1672x941 canvas, no zoom. Rotate this rear-facing man ONLY 15 degrees farther toward screen RIGHT, so most of the BACK remains visible and only his right ear, a very narrow cheek sliver and barely the tip of his nose show at screen-right edge of his head. Absolutely NO eye contact with viewer; eyes are NOT visible. His torso is still 70 percent rear view. Keep hands and baton almost exactly in the same places; lower the baton tip only 30 pixels. This is the very next pose, not the final pose. No new objects, no text, no background. Keep original head height and position and same total figure height.
corrections.6: Edit the reference into the next animation pose of the SAME man. Preserve EXACT canvas, camera distance, identity, warm copper/espresso oil paint style, clothes, alpha transparency and lower body scale. Single pose on original 1672x941 canvas, no zoom. Turn the man to a STRICT RIGHT-FACING SIDE PROFILE: nose points horizontally to screen RIGHT. Show exactly ONE eye looking to the right, not at viewer; NO front-facing face, NO second eye. Torso also is side-on, narrow side of suit visible, jacket back still slightly visible at left. Right elbow stays bent near ribs, right baton hand at x1180 y480, baton extending near-horizontal toward screen right. Left hand remains relaxed near chest, partially hidden. Body remains upright, hair top at y110, head width about170px and same hips position. This is a true side-view intermediary, not the final three-quarter front view. No new objects, no text, no background. Keep original head height and position and same total figure height.
